body.x: Organizations that want staff to reach Windows applications and desktops from any device and location have traditionally relied on remote desktop infrastructure, which can be costly and inflexible to run.
TSplus positions its software as a lower-cost, more flexible alternative.

TSplus SAS, a French software company founded in 2007 and headquartered in Paris, specializes in secure remote access, remote desktop and Windows application delivery. Represented in Korea by Country Director Mariam Essafi, the company is exhibiting four solutions at KES 2026 and aims to meet potential distributors, resellers, system integrators and technology partners there.

TSplus Remote Access, the flagship product, lets organizations publish Windows applications and desktops and access them remotely on-premises or in the cloud. TSplus Remote Support provides secure remote assistance for IT teams, TSplus Server Monitoring tracks the performance, availability and health of servers and services, and TSplus Advanced Security protects Windows servers and remote access environments against unauthorized access. The company says the four products give businesses a single suite of tools for managing remote IT infrastructure.

TSplus reports revenue of about USD 12 million in 2025, with average annual growth of around 20%. It has 80 employees at its headquarters and branches in the Czech Republic, the United States, India and China, and says it serves more than 500,000 customers and 5 million users in over 170 countries through a network of more than 7,000 resellers. Customers include HD Hyundai, Siemens, LG Electronics, Magic Software and Skyone. In France, it recently formed partnerships with IONOS and Dassault Systèmes.

South Korea is a strategic market for TSplus because of its advanced IT infrastructure and high adoption of cloud and digital solutions. The company also wants to expand in Japan and build out its partner network across Asia-Pacific. It is looking for distributors, IT resellers, system integrators, managed service providers (MSPs) and cloud service providers with technical expertise, established B2B networks and the ability to provide local sales and support.

The company would particularly welcome introductions to qualified Korean distributors, resellers and system integrators, as well as opportunities to raise its profile in the local market. Introductions to qualified Korean distributors, resellers and integrators, and opportunities to build local visibility, are the support it names as most valuable.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
